candidates.statement: Use listing platforms mainly to discover places and carry the communication on outside the apps.
context: Current practice, described as usual

evidence_candidates.quote: So I mainly use this type of platforms like as a way to discover places. But I actually usually proceed with different type of communication outside of these apps.

candidates.statement: See when a listing's information was last updated so that I can be assured it is current.
context: Because the information may be outdated or wrong

evidence_candidates.quote: You don't know when was the time the information was lastly updated. There are no such information. It might be like outdated.
Also, another thing that I would really love is to have to be able to see when it was last updated.
It just. I just want to be assured that it's it's up to date.

candidates.statement: See a timeline of the next steps and of what to expect after an inquiry, including what happens if it fails.
context: Would make the stakeholder more comfortable and more willing to engage

evidence_candidates.quote: and I can see, like a small visual of the timeline that, like the website, can show me what are the next steps. If I fail, therefore, what should I expect?
I would love like to know if I just proceeded with this option, what will happen when they would they respond to me? What will be next?

So maybe it's changing something in in the ui to make the user have some insight about, how would the communication process be? This will make him like, trust the feature more, and never try something else, and just keep the communication in in the website.

candidates.statement: Contact a provider with a short message instead of a long mandatory form and without handing over all personal details up front.
context: The current form requires first name, last name, email, mobile, move dates, beds, baths and a custom message

evidence_candidates.quote: you will have this long form that you don't know how it will be submitted
and all of them are required fields, and you still don't know a lot about the one who is providing this house, so it doesn't feel very comfortable to give all this information
You just have a vague button called. Send a message where you will fill a form and never know what will happen next.

candidates.statement: Share personal details only after both sides confirm availability and interest.
context: Before that confirmation the information is not considered necessary

evidence_candidates.quote: I think like giving the information could be after confirming the availability from the 2 parties like if they said, this apartment is available, and I said, I'm interested.
before that step I think it's not necessary to give all the information

candidates.statement: Pick a specific available unit from the listed options instead of writing a custom message.
context: Housing options are limited and not customised, unlike made-to-order goods

evidence_candidates.quote: Sometimes you don't want to write a custom message. You just want to pick the available option you like.
they can just list it with their specification, and I can have something similar to the concept of. Add to cart

candidates.statement: Search and use the full functionality without being required to register or log in, keeping registration optional for saving information.
context: Registration is acceptable only as an option to save details and autofill

evidence_candidates.quote: Maybe he could. It could be optional thing like if you want your information saved and to be filled directly you can register. But it should not be required.
Just start searching and seeing the whole functionality directly.

candidates.statement: Search the information I want conveniently, without steps I do not consider beneficial.
context: Stated as the primary goal behind skipping login

evidence_candidates.quote: It's like to be more convenient just to search the information you want without having steps that you don't believe it's beneficial.

candidates.statement: Keep the interface to few, clearly understood actions and avoid unknown buttons or extra steps.
context: Unknown extra steps make the stakeholder leave the site

evidence_candidates.quote: one of the things that I don't like is actually these extra steps like requiring you to register in the website. And then you have, like, multiple, unknown, like multiple buttons that you don't know. What would they proceed you to?
this type of long, unknown process makes me just skip the website and look for a website with like minimal options and and list things to do.

candidates.statement: Select the search area by drawing a circle on a map instead of relying only on neighborhood names.
context: Neighborhood-name search is too specific and misses nearby options

evidence_candidates.quote: One of the things that I like is that they provide sometimes a map with a drawing tool where you can just draw a circle around the place you're interested in in the map
because sometimes searching by the neighborhood name will be very specific, like, if there is a very good option just 2 meters away, it will not be considered

candidates.statement: Read reviews from people about a place so that it feels more trusted and the information sits together.

evidence_candidates.quote: Also, another thing that I like is providing reviews, I think reviews from people, makes. makes places feel more trusted, and could help let you have all the information together.

candidates.statement: Compare three or four liked options on a single page with their main features side by side.
context: The stakeholder has not found a website that offers this

evidence_candidates.quote: I wish, if there is an option for comparison, like, sometimes I like 3 or 4 options like, I want to collect them all in in like a single page. So I can look in the main features at the same time.
I just want to mention it again about comparing between several options like, I wish, if there is such feature that helps me to compare

candidates.statement: Save interesting options to a favorites list that can be found from the nav bar or the first level of the menu.
context: Currently the saved items cannot be located after saving

evidence_candidates.quote: there is a button called favorites. It should like, I assume as a normal user that if I click on favorites it should save the thing I'm looking for. But actually, I can't find where where it's saving it.
It should be like on the nav bar, or at least at the menu, at the like 1st level of the menu.

candidates.statement: Avoid losing suitable options whose attributes the provider left unspecified when filtering.
context: Example: an owner may allow pets without stating it in the profile

evidence_candidates.quote: What if I filter by some criteria, and then I lost all the options where the owners didn't specify.
because sometimes I have this fear that maybe I filtered by something, and I missed options that were not entered appropriately.

candidates.statement: Keep the filters optional rather than forcing the user to fill every field.
context: Sometimes the stakeholder is not sure what he wants

evidence_candidates.quote: I like that. The filters are optional. They don't enforce you to enter everything, because sometimes you're not very assured about what do you want

candidates.statement: Include listings that did not specify a criterion when the user asks for it, for example through a checkbox, so that both confirmed and unspecified options are shown.
context: Without the checkbox only listings that confirm the criterion are shown

evidence_candidates.quote: maybe if there is like a check box called include, for example, like the options that didn't determine, or something like that.
The one who allowed and the one who didn't specify, and if I didn't click on the checkbox, I will have the ones who only specify that they allow.

candidates.statement: Have the website enforce a standard photo format (light and angles) for listings so that the photos are more trustworthy.
context: Proposed tentatively ('maybe'); expected effect is more trust in the site

evidence_candidates.quote: maybe if the website has some sort of rules that enforces people who own these properties to take the picture in a specific format, for example, on, for example, sunlight using like specific angles. Maybe this will give people more trust to use a website over another one.

candidates.statement: Keep all housing communication with property owners inside the website, provided the process is clear and fast.
context: Condition: the communication process is clear and fast
The stakeholder wants to decide within a week or at most a month

evidence_candidates.quote: it will be very sufficient to communicate with the property owners through these websites. If the process was clear and fast. It will be so good like to have all the communication through a single platform.
This will make him like, trust the feature more, and never try something else, and just keep the communication in in the website.

review_questions.question: “搬迁时找到新住处”是流程的触发情境，作为独立目标是否过泛？
review_questions.reason: 它更像整段流程的目的背景，可能不承载独立验收维度。

review_questions.question: 以“maybe”提出的照片格式规则，是否应保持为暂定建议而不作为承诺？
review_questions.reason: 语气为试探性建议，采纳与否未知。

limitations: 转写稿含口语重复、断句与自我更正，引文按原文逐字复制，未做语言润色。
仅依据本任务分配的原文判断，未联网检索，也未参考其他资料或历史结果。
个别窗口（如 W0031–W0034 的细节页问答）以确认现状为主，未产生新目标。
支持标签为生成方判断，未执行独立语义评审与形式证明。
